name: refraction
description: Light crossing the boundary between two media (air, water, glass…): the dashed normal, the incident ray from its lamp, the refracted ray bent by Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, the partly reflected ray (as strong as the physics says), and θ₁, θ₂ marked with arcs and values — all computed. Choose it for ANY request about refraction, Snell's law, refractive index, why a straw looks bent or a pool looks shallow, the critical angle, total internal reflection (fibre optics, diamonds), or a glass slab's sideways shift. Past the critical angle (n₁ > n₂) the refracted ray is gone and only reflection remains. theta1_deg, n1 and n2 ANIMATE: {"animate": {"theta1_deg": 60}, "duration": 4} from water into air sweeps past the critical angle. Paused, the viewer drags the lamp or any ray (the angles follow), scrubs or types n = 1.33 and θ₁/θ₂; an explore beat naming nothing invites exactly this. Numbers for text: {refraction.theta1}, {refraction.theta2} (absent past the critical angle), {refraction.critical}, {refraction.n1}, {refraction.n2}, {refraction.reflected} (percent), {refraction.v1}/{refraction.v2} (speed as a fraction of c), {refraction.shift} (slab, in thicknesses), {refraction.depth_ratio} (apparent).
interaction: Drag the lamp or a ray to aim the light; scrub a medium's n or an angle; Snell's law solves the rest.

medium1.description: Where the light comes from, e.g. "air" (default) — a word or two, in the cast's language.

n1.description: Its refractive index — always give it (air 1.00, water 1.33, glass 1.50, diamond 2.42).

theta1_deg.description: Angle of incidence from the normal, 0–89.5 (default 40). Animates.

from.description: Side the lamp is on (default left).

light_from.description: "below": medium1 is drawn under the boundary and the light goes up (the straw: water below, eye above).

show_angles.description: Arcs and values for θ₁ and θ₂ (default true).

show_reflection.description: The partial reflected ray (default true; always drawn past the critical angle).

show_critical.description: The critical angle as a dashed line with its value when n1 > n2 (default true).

show_law.description: Write n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ with the live numbers (default false).

wavefronts.description: Crests across the rays, closer together where light is slower (default false).

apparent.description: The refracted ray traced straight back (dashed) to where the lamp APPEARS to be — the bent straw, the shallow pool.

image_label.description: Text by the apparent position (default "appears here").

eye.description: An eye at the end of the ray, looking back along it.

slab.description: medium2 is a slab with medium1 again beyond it: the ray leaves parallel, shifted sideways.

source_label.description: A word or two by the lamp, e.g. "straw tip".

element_ids.medium1 / medium2: the two media's washes (deeper for a higher index), with medium1_name / medium2_name and n1_label / n2_label ("n = 1.33") at the left edge
element_ids.normal: the dashed normal through the point where the ray meets the boundary
element_ids.source: the lamp the incident ray starts from (source_label beside it when given)
element_ids.incident_ray / refracted_ray / reflected: the rays (refracted_ray absent past the critical angle)
element_ids.theta2_arc / theta2_label: θ₂'s arc and value (absent past the critical angle)
element_ids.angles: SET — the arcs and their values
element_ids.critical_line / critical_label: the critical angle, dashed, with "θc = 48.8°" (n1 > n2)
element_ids.tir_label: "Total internal reflection", past the critical angle
element_ids.law / law_numbers: Snell's law and the same with the live numbers (show_law)
element_ids.apparent_ray / image / image_label: the ray traced back, where the lamp appears, its words (apparent)
element_ids.boundary2 / medium3 / medium3_name / nor: the slab's far side and the ray out of it (slab)
element_ids.incident_extension / shift_arrow / shift: the incident ray carried straight on and the sideways shift (slab)
element_ids.title: the title, when set

examples.request: How does light bend going from air into water?
When does light stop getting out of water?
Why does a straw look bent in water?
Why does a glass slab shift a ray sideways?
